item.text: I’ve hit the search limit for this lens and am synthesizing from the strongest material available: health-system response, displacement support, and crisis-management evidence on the positive side, plus conflict, aid diversion, and emergency-rule harms on the negative side.

**Bottom line:** Mixed, leaning no. I found meaningful crisis-mitigation steps in health financing, food/cash support, reconstruction, and refugee/IDP programs. But the strongest 2024 operational evidence is still severe: food-aid diversion, attacks on medical care, mass detention under emergency rule, and repeated harm to displaced people. That undercuts a claim that Abiy’s government broadly reduced avoidable suffering during crises.

**Positive evidence**
- **Ethiopia Country Profile 2024** | **World Health Organization** | **2024** | https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2024-2025/country-profile/2024/ethiopia  
  WHO says it supported Ethiopia to strengthen primary health care, improve service delivery, and track health expenditures and barriers so decision-makers could respond to financial hardship. This is indirect but real evidence of a measurement-based crisis response infrastructure.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.5`, `6B.4`

- **Ethiopia: Request for an Arrangement Under the Extended Credit Facility** | **International Monetary Fund** | **2024-07-29** | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24291-ethiopia-imf-exec-board-approves-4yr-us3b-ecf-arr  
  The IMF says the package included expanding PSNP cash transfers, temporary fuel and fertilizer subsidies, and public investment management for post-conflict reconstruction. That is strong evidence of active shock cushioning during inflation and crisis conditions.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`

- **Bringing Back More Schools, Health Facilities to Life in Tigray** | **United Nations in Ethiopia** | **2024-02-23** | https://ethiopia.un.org/en/261479-bringing-back-more-schools-health-facilities-life-tigray  
  The project reconstructed 14 health centers, 11 schools, and 33 WASH facilities for 365,000 people in five woredas. This is concrete evidence of reducing suffering in a conflict-affected area by restoring basic services.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Second Phase of PROSPECTS Launched in Ethiopia** | **UNICEF Ethiopia** | **2024-03-21** | https://www.unicef.org/ethiopia/press-releases/second-phase-prospects-launched-ethiopia-empowering-refugees-idps-and-host  
  UNICEF and partners launched support for refugees, IDPs, and host communities through education, livelihoods, protection, and infrastructure. This is direct crisis-displacement mitigation, though programmatic and limited in scale.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Ethiopia Launches National Strategy to Implement Solutions Pathways for Internal Displacement** | **UN Ethiopia / UNHCR** | **2024-11-11** | https://ethiopia.un.org/en/283776-ethiopia-launches-national-strategy-implement-solutions-pathways-internal-displacement  
  The government and UN launched a strategy for voluntary return, local integration, reintegration, coordination, and accountability for IDPs. This is the clearest positive institutional evidence for reducing displacement-related suffering, though it is a strategy launch rather than outcome proof.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.5`

- **Gov’t Vows to Strengthen Health Financing to Further Improve Ethiopia’s Health Services** | **ENA English** | **2024-10-03** | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5233579  
  The ministry said health insurance coverage improved and financial barriers to primary care fell, which is direct evidence of reducing avoidable suffering through better health-financing management.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`

- **World Bank scales up efforts to boost the resilience of 3 million AFE Ethiopians living in drought-prone lowlands** | **World Bank** | **2024-03-29** | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/03/29/world-bank-scales-up-efforts-to-boost-the-resilience-of-3-million-afe-ethiopians-living-in-drought-prone-lowlands  
  The Bank said 3 million people in drought-prone lowlands would receive resilience support, explicitly linking the need to drought, floods, conflict, and environmental degradation. This is indirect but relevant evidence of crisis-suffering reduction in vulnerable regions.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

**Negative evidence**
- **World Report 2024: Ethiopia** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024** | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia  
  HRW says a coordinated aid-diversion scheme led WFP and USAID to halt food aid, sharply restricting access for about 20 million people. That is strong evidence of failed crisis relief and possible capture or patronage interference.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`

- **Ethiopia Military Executes Dozens in Amhara Region** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-04-04** | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region  
  HRW reported federal forces summarily killed dozens of civilians in Merawi. This is direct evidence that state action in crisis zones was producing avoidable suffering rather than reducing it.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.3`, `6B.2`

- **Ethiopia Army Attacks Health Care in Amhara Conflict** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-07-03** | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/03/ethiopia-army-attacks-health-care-amhara-conflict  
  HRW documented seizures of ambulances, raids on hospitals, arrests of medical staff, and attacks on medical neutrality. That is strong evidence against crisis-suffering reduction for the wounded and sick.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Ethiopia Fighting Abuses Putting Sudanese Refugees at Risk** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-10-17** | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/17/ethiopia-fighting-abuses-putting-sudanese-refugees-risk  
  HRW said Sudanese refugees in camps faced killings, beatings, looting, forced labor, and unsafe relocation pressure. That is strong evidence that a highly vulnerable displaced population was not adequately protected.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.3`, `6B.2`

- **End the Month-Long Arbitrary Detention of Thousands in Amhara Region** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-11-06** | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/ethiopia-end-the-month-long-arbitrary-detention-of-thousands-in-amhara-region/  
  Amnesty reported thousands of civilians were rounded up into makeshift detention camps. This suggests coercive crisis control, not suffering reduction.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.3`, `6B.5`

- **Ethiopia extends state of emergency in Amhara** | **Reuters via KELO** | **2024-02-02** | https://kelo.com/2024/02/02/ethiopia-extends-state-of-emergency-in-amhara/  
  Reuters described emergency rule amid insurgency, deaths, and abuse allegations. This is negative crisis context: the government was relying on coercive emergency management in a deteriorating security environment.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.6`, also `6B.5`, `6B.2`

**Search gap**
- I did not find a strong 2024 source showing Abiy’s government ran a transparent, publicly measurable crisis-response system across all major shocks, or a clear pandemic-specific response in 2024. The evidence is fragmented: some real mitigation in health, food, displacement, and reconstruction, but broad crisis suffering remained severe and often worsened by state violence or breakdowns in protection.
